title: Set 79

sentences.ko: 토요일에 오빠네 집까지 차로 가려고 했는데, 이제 와서 눈이 아니라 얼음이 온대. 어두울 때 그 길로는 운전 안 해. 그래서 일요일로 미뤘더니 오빠가 벌써 나한테 짜증 났어. 2월에도 내가 똑같이 그랬거든.
sentences.text: We were going to drive up to my brother's on Saturday, but now they're saying it's going to be ice, not snow, and I'm not doing that road in the dark. So we pushed it to Sunday and he's already annoyed with me, because I did the exact same thing to him back in February.

alts.text: Saturday we were supposed to head up to my brother's, but now they're saying ice, not snow, and I'm not driving that road in the dark. So we bumped it to Sunday and he's already annoyed with me, cause I pulled the exact same thing on him back in February.

We had planned to drive up to my brother's house on Saturday, but the forecast is now calling for ice rather than snow, and I am not willing to take that road after dark. We have moved it to Sunday, and he is already irritated with me, because I did exactly the same thing to him back in February.

sentences.note: **pushed it to Sunday** 는 약속을 일요일로 미뤘다는 말. **I'm not doing that road in the dark** 처럼 do 를 쓰면 그 길을 어두울 때 운전하는 일 자체를 안 하겠다는 뜻이 된다.

sentences.ko: 봄까지만 버티자고 스스로 계속 되뇌는데, 이번 주처럼 한 주 몰아치면 밤 열한 시에 또 현장에 나가 있어. 일 자체에 문제가 있는 건 아니야. 그게 아내한테 설명이 안 되는 부분이고. 너라면 멀쩡한 일을 그만두겠어?
sentences.text: I keep telling myself I'll stick it out till spring, and then a week like this one happens and I'm on the job sites again at eleven at night. Nothing's actually wrong with the job, and that's the part I can't explain to my wife. Would you leave something that's fine?

alts.text: Every time I say I'll just hang on till spring, then a week like this hits and I'm back on the job sites at eleven at night. There's nothing actually wrong with the job, and that's the part I can't get across to my wife. Would you quit something that's fine?

I keep telling myself that I will remain until spring, and then a week like this one comes along and I am back on the job sites at eleven at night. There is nothing genuinely wrong with the position, and that is the part I cannot explain to my wife. Would you leave something that is perfectly fine?

sentences.note: **stick it out** 은 힘들어도 정해 둔 때까지 버틴다는 뜻. **that's the part I can't explain** 은 다른 건 다 말이 되는데 그 대목만 설명이 안 된다는 말이다.

sentences.ko: 담임 선생님이 읽기 문제로 또 메일을 보내셨어. 솔직히 나는 애가 괜찮다고 생각해. 그냥 애들 앞에서 소리 내서 읽는 게 싫은 거지. 너희 애도 그런 적 있었어? 학교에서는 소그룹 수업에 넣자고 하는데, 그게 애한테 도움이 될지 아니면 그냥 수업 중에 불려 나가는 애가 돼 버릴지 모르겠어.
sentences.text: His teacher emailed me about the reading again, and honestly I think he's fine, he just doesn't want to do it out loud in front of everybody. Did yours go through that? Because they want to put him in the small group, and I don't know if that helps him or if he just becomes the kid who gets pulled out.

alts.text: Got another email from his teacher about the reading, and honestly I think he's fine, he just doesn't wanna do it out loud in front of everybody. Did yours go through that? Cause they wanna stick him in the small group, and I dunno if that actually helps him or if he just turns into the kid who gets pulled out.

His teacher emailed me about the reading again, and in all honesty I believe he is fine. He simply does not want to read aloud in front of everyone. Did your child go through that as well? They would like to place him in the small group, and I do not know whether that would help him or whether he would simply become the child who gets taken out of class.

sentences.note: **gets pulled out** 은 수업 도중에 따로 불려 나간다는 뜻으로 학교 얘기에서 자주 쓴다. **Did yours go through that?** 의 yours 는 상대방 아이를 가리킨다.

sentences.ko: 그 사람은 내 사촌이랑 같이 사는 사람인데 간호사야. 일주일에 사흘은 밤 근무라 시간 맞추기가 좀 애매한 건 나도 알아. 처음 십 분만 지나면 은근히 웃긴 사람인데, 대화를 알아서 끌어 주지는 않아. 그러니까 그래 주기를 가만히 앉아서 기다리면 저녁 시간이 길게 느껴질 거야. 나라면 그냥 술 한잔 하면서 어떤가 보겠어.
sentences.text: So he's my cousin's roommate, he's a nurse, and he works nights three days a week, which I know is a weird schedule to work around. He's actually funny once you get past the first ten minutes, but he's not going to carry the conversation for you, so if you sit there waiting for him to do that it'll be a long dinner. I'd just meet him for a drink and see what happens.

alts.text: Okay so he rooms with my cousin, he's a nurse, and he's on nights three days a week, which yeah, that's a weird schedule to plan around. He's actually funny once you're past the first ten minutes, but he's not gonna carry the conversation for you, so if you sit there waiting on that it's gonna be a long dinner. I'd just grab a drink with him and see how it goes.

He is my cousin's roommate, he works as a nurse, and he works nights three days a week, which I realize is an awkward schedule to accommodate. He is genuinely funny once you get past the first ten minutes, but he will not carry the conversation for you, so if you sit there waiting for him to do so it will be a long dinner. I would simply meet him for a drink and see what happens.

sentences.note: **carry the conversation** 은 말이 끊기지 않게 혼자 대화를 끌고 간다는 뜻. **a weird schedule to work around** 의 work around 는 그 일정에 맞춰 내 쪽을 조정한다는 말이다.
sentences.situation: 친구 소개팅 주선하면서 상대가 어떤 사람인지 설명하기

sentences.ko: 예전엔 5달러에 사 먹던 샌드위치를 9달러 주고 샀어. 크기가 더 커진 것도 아닌데. 그러고도 결국 샀으니 내가 뭐라 할 처지는 아니지. 그래도 요즘은 물건값을 진짜로 들여다보게 됐어. 예전에는 안 그랬거든.
sentences.text: I paid nine dollars for the same sandwich I used to get for five, and it's not like they made it any bigger. And I still bought it, so I don't really have a leg to stand on here. But I've started actually looking at what things cost, and I never used to do that.

alts.text: Nine bucks for the same sandwich that used to run me five, and it's not like it got any bigger. And I bought it anyway, so I can't really talk here. But I've started actually checking what stuff costs, and I never used to do that.

I paid nine dollars for the same sandwich I used to buy for five, and they have not made it any larger. And I purchased it regardless, so I am hardly in a position to complain. But I have begun paying attention to what things cost, and I never used to do that.

sentences.note: **have a leg to stand on** 은 자기 말을 뒷받침할 근거가 있다는 뜻이라, 부정으로 쓰면 따질 처지가 아니라는 말이 된다. **it's not like** 은 그렇다고 그런 것도 아니잖아 하고 덧붙일 때 쓴다.

reviewed: 1번 한국어: 'I'm not doing that road in the dark' 는 안 하겠다는 단언인데 '운전하고 싶진 않아' 로 눅여 놓아서 '어두울 때 그 길로는 운전 안 해' 로 고쳤다. annoyed 도 '화가 났어' 보다 '짜증 났어' 가 맞아 바꿨다.
2번 한국어: '이번 주 같은 주가 닥치면' 이 번역투라 '이번 주처럼 한 주 몰아치면' 으로, '나 스스로한테 계속 말하는데' 도 '스스로 계속 되뇌는데' 로 다듬었다.
2번 formal: 'a week like this one occurs' 는 격식체라도 사람이 안 쓰는 말이라 'comes along' 으로 바꿨다.
3번 한국어: '소수 그룹 수업' 은 안 쓰는 말이라 '소그룹 수업' 으로 고쳤다.
3번 formal: 세미콜론으로 이은 자리를 소리내어 읽기 좋게 마침표로 끊었다.
